item.title: Premature baby fighting for his life amid the COVID-19 pandemic
item.description: SAN ANTONIO (WOAI/KABB) — The COVID-19 crisis is adding more struggles for a family with a premature baby fighting for his life. Right now, Maximus Diaz is starting a new breathing treatment to try to help his lungs which are severely underdeveloped. He was born on June 17 after only 24 weeks and 5 days in the womb. Caption: WOAI. He’s been in the hospital for two months. Maximus had severe uterine growth restrictions, which means, he was not getting enough nutrients or blood from the placenta.

item.title: Researchers say COVID-19 could have been in U.S. back in December 2019 based on data
item.description: NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WZTV) — New research from doctors at UCLA's David Geffen School of Medicine and the UW School of Public Health in Seattle estimates SARS-CoV-2 could have been in the United States as far back as December. The researchers examined U. S. health system data representing 2. 5 million patient visits each year from July 2014 to February 29, 2020. They then examined the number of excess hospital visits and clinic visits last winter and compared it to previous seasons.
